Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.internal.swingnode

Class SwingNodeWindowCapture

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.internal.swingnode.SwingNodeWindowCapture
public final class SwingNodeWindowCapture extends Object
Global registry that lets a SwingNode capture and render the top-level Swing windows an unmodified application creates - JOptionPane and JFileChooser dialogs, custom JDialog/JWindow popups, and a conventional app's own JFrames - instead of letting them pop onto the host desktop where the offscreen texture capture cannot reach them.

One AWTEventListener is installed lazily on the first registration and watches every WINDOW_EVENT_MASK event in the JVM:

  • A newly opened JFrame (other than a SwingNode's own hidden frame and the desktop host window) is handed to CapturedFrameHost so it becomes a real desktop window.
  • A newly opened JDialog/JWindow is attributed to the SwingNode that owns it (via the owner chain, else the last-active node), parked off-screen, and recorded as a centred overlay that the node paints into its texture and routes input to. Modal semantics are preserved because a modal dialog runs its own secondary EDT loop, which processes the events the node's renderer dispatches on the EDT.

This class is an implementation detail of SwingNode and must not be instantiated by users; every member is static.

  • Method Details

    • registerHiddenFrame

      public static void registerHiddenFrame(Window hiddenFrame, SwingNode node)
      Registers a SwingNode's hidden frame so its own window is never captured and so dialogs it owns can be attributed back to the node. Installs the global window hook on the first call.

    • unregisterHiddenFrame

      public static void unregisterHiddenFrame(Window hiddenFrame)
      Unregisters a SwingNode's hidden frame (called from dispose()).

    • setLastActiveNode

      public static void setLastActiveNode(SwingNode node)
      Records the node the pointer is currently over so an owner-less dialog (e.g. JOptionPane.showConfirmDialog(null, ...)) can be attributed to a window instead of escaping to the host desktop.

    • registerFullBleed

      public static void registerFullBleed(SwingNode node, Window window)
      Registers window as a full-bleed capture of node: the node paints it as its entire texture at origin (0,0) and routes all input to it. Used by CapturedFrameHost to present a conventional app's JFrame as a desktop window.

    • releaseNode

      public static void releaseNode(SwingNode node)
      Removes every capture associated with node (called on dispose).

    • getCaptured

      public static List<Window> getCaptured(SwingNode node)
      Returns the windows node should paint as overlays, in paint order (topmost last). Never null; safe to iterate on the EDT.

    • getOverlayOrigin

      public static Point getOverlayOrigin(SwingNode node, Window window, int panelW, int panelH)
      Returns the top-left origin, in the hosting panel's pixel space, where window should be painted. Full-bleed captures sit at (0,0); dialogs are centred within the panelW x panelH area and clamped so they never start at a negative offset.

    • getNodeForWindow

      public static SwingNode getNodeForWindow(Window window)
      Returns the node presenting window (or any window up its owner chain) so the SwingNode repaint manager can mark it dirty when a captured dialog repaints. Returns null when the component is unrelated.

    • resolveInputTarget

      public static SwingNodeWindowCapture.InputTarget resolveInputTarget(SwingNode node, Point panelPos, int panelW, int panelH)
      Resolves where a forwarded input event aimed at panel-space panelPos should go. When the node has a captured modal dialog, ALL input is routed to it (modal semantics). Otherwise a captured overlay whose rect contains panelPos receives the event with local coordinates. Returns null when no captured window applies, meaning the caller should fall back to the node's own hidden frame.

    • ensureHookInstalled

      public static void ensureHookInstalled()
      Ensures the global window hook is installed even before any SwingNode exists. A conventional Swing app launched in-JVM from the start menu can open its JFrame before the desktop has created a SwingNode (StickyNote, the only start-up-path node, is created lazily on window flip), so without this the frame would escape to the host desktop. Called once from DisplayServerControl after start-up completes. Idempotent.

    • registerCapturePackage

      public static void registerCapturePackage(String mainClassName)
      Registers an app (by its main class name) for 3D window capture: the class's package becomes a prefix, and any top-level JFrame whose class is in that package will be captured and presented as a desktop window. Called by the launchers for apps that opt in (the swingapp command verb or -Dlg.swingapp). Apps that do not opt in keep their normal host windows and native input.
